latest_checkpoint: Phase 8 (Windows Quick Start support) is complete as of 2026-10-25 (Session 6): windows-desktop-windows-container-readiness (read-only engine-mode probe in desktop + `GET /docker/engine`; Create screen enables templates per engine mode, Windows readiness panel with Docker/Microsoft links and Retry, gate 'Container engine' check, import hands mismatches to the gate, Practicum never switches the mode), designer-windows-quick-start (spec `Node.os`/`Node.shell`; Windows Server Core template pinned from a host-build compatibility matrix, PowerShell keep-alive init passed as -EncodedCommand, `nat` networks, server-side engine re-check with switch instructions), windows-desktop-open-windows-shell (shell from the declared os/shell, 'Open PowerShell', pre-check for stopped/missing containers), designer-windows-quick-start-packages (Chocolatey tool catalog + custom ids, per-package install with a status marker read by /status), and windows-desktop-design-icons (design/icons.png sliced into assets, shared icons.py, MessageBanner/StatusPill/buttons/markers across every screen, packaging add-data). Tests: core 204, desktop 350, all green (incl. a cross-package contract test validating the desktop-built Windows lab with the core model); e2e against the live API with a stateful fake docker CLI (Linux-mode refusal -> switch -> start -> running with install note -> lifecycle -> export/import). The three pre-existing test_docker_status failures (creationflags) are fixed. NOTHING FROM SESSIONS 5 AND 6 HAS RUN ON WINDOWS YET - next: the Windows smoke run (Tigre/05 checklist, now including Docker Desktop in Windows-container mode: Server Core pull, Open PowerShell, Chocolatey install). Still open afterwards: Tigre/11 S-1 persistence, S-2/S-3 packaging supervision, S-8/S-9 designer depth, S-14 stable lab identity. Addendum (user request, same day): the Custom Lab designer gained a Lab instructions panel with a student-view preview (designer-author-manual's designer half; shared manual_editor.py). Scope change (same day, stories only): Windows-container labs are to move behind the paid tier because they need Windows Pro/Enterprise/Education; see src/future-roadmap/premium-lab-platforms/ (7 stories incl. a macOS counterpart, D-50). Nothing built was removed. Persistence planning (2026-10-26): selected local SQLite with a per-user Windows app-data location and a development path override; Phase 9 stories drafted for durable lab records, Docker startup reconciliation, and data-directory configuration. Implementation not started. Website planning (2026-10-26): added Phase 10 with stories for product positioning, release downloads, getting started, and project transparency/contribution. Website implementation and hosting are not started.

stories.title: Subnet Conflict Detection and Resolution
stories.notes: Added and implemented 2026-10-23 after the first Windows smoke run of the import flow failed at start with Docker's 'Pool overlaps with other one on this address space' (Tigre/06 #13; was Tigre/11 proposal S-16). Core: src/practicum/networks.py (find_subnet_conflicts / recommend_subnet from 10.90.0.0/16 / move_subnet keeping host offsets), DockerRuntime.list_networks() (docker network ls + inspect, parses IPAM subnets, practicum.lab_id label, attached containers) and remove_network() (docker rm -f containers, then network rm), LabService.check_networks / apply_subnet_recommendation / remove_leftover_network, routes GET /labs/{id}/networks, POST /labs/{id}/networks/apply-recommendation, POST /labs/{id}/networks/remove-leftover (409 for no recommendation / not a leftover), models DockerNetworkInfo, SubnetConflict (reasons overlaps_other_lab | overlaps_leftover | overlaps_docker_network), NetworkCheckResult (error field when Docker is unreachable), and LabDefinition now rejects overlapping subnets within a lab. Desktop: ApiClient.check_networks / apply_subnet_recommendation / remove_leftover_network / reset_lab; PreStartGateDialog gained a 'Network Conflicts' group (owner text per reason; fixes 'Remove leftover' and 'Reset <lab>' via confirm(destructive=True), 'Use <subnet>' which re-renders the topology and warns that the manual may mention old addresses; Start requires both port and network checks to have answered clean); ImportLabDialog's check stage is now 'Checking host ports and networks…' and hands over to the gate on subnet conflicts. Tests: core +27 (test_networks 11, test_network_conflicts_api 11 with a FakeRuntime, test_runtime +5), desktop +17 (gate +8, api_client +7, import +2). Verified end-to-end in the sandbox against a stateful fake docker CLI: the user's exact failure reproduced, then all three fixes (remove leftover, reset owner, use subnet) cleared it and the lab started. Not yet verified on Windows with real Docker Desktop. Update 2026-10-24: apply-recommendation (move_subnet) also rewrites the moved addresses in the manual (networks.rewrite_addresses) — stale 'ping 10.93.1.20' text after a move was the likely cause of a reported 100 % packet loss.

acceptance_criteria.text: A lab whose subnet overlaps an existing Docker network is reported by GET /labs/{lab_id}/networks with the owner identified and a recommended subnet, before any Start is attempted.

Applying the recommended subnet moves the network and its addresses, the topology shown in the gate updates, and the user is told the manual may still mention the old addresses.

Canceling a delete confirmation leaves the lab list unchanged.

stories.title: Pre-Start Readiness Gate
stories.notes: Implemented as PreStartGateDialog (desktop/src/practicum_desktop/prestart_gate.py): loads GET /labs/{lab_id}/preview and GET /labs/{lab_id}/ports in parallel, shows name/description/author/version, required images, estimated CPU/memory, a read-only topology table (node/network/address), a manual step count, and a port-conflicts table with per-row 'Use <port>' buttons. Start Lab is disabled while conflicts remain and re-enables once resolved. Wired into main_window.py's existing Start button (which now opens this dialog instead of calling start_lab directly); the main window's Start button and inline port-conflict table no longer gate on conflicts themselves, since the dialog is now the single authority for that. Required extending PreviewResult/get_preview in api_client.py to parse required_images/estimated_resources/topology fields the API already returned but the desktop client was discarding. 11 new tests (7 dialog + 4 extended api_client assertions implicitly covered by existing suite), all passing; PORT_CONFLICT_REASONS moved to api_client.py as a shared constant to avoid duplicating it between main_window.py and this dialog. Not yet reachable from the Labs Dashboard or Import flows since those don't exist yet (windows-desktop-labs-dashboard, windows-desktop-import-lab-file) - both should open this same dialog rather than re-implementing the gate once built. Update 2026-10-23: the gate now also checks Docker subnet overlaps (GET /labs/{id}/networks) in a 'Network Conflicts' group with Remove leftover / Reset <lab> / Use <subnet> fixes; Start requires both the port and the network check to be clean (runtime-subnet-conflicts).

acceptance_criteria.text: The screen shows lab name, description, required images, estimated resources, and read-only topology.
Port conflicts block Start until resolved, and applying a recommendation re-checks and clears that conflict.
A lab with zero conflicts shows a clear ready-to-start state and an immediately-enabled Start button.
Canceling this screen does not start, modify, or delete the lab.

stories.title: Import Lab File and Launch
stories.notes: Implemented 2026-10-23 as ImportLabDialog in desktop/src/practicum_desktop/import_lab.py, opened from the new 'Import Lab File…' button in main_window.py. The dialog is the in-app 'Open Lab File' modal from the mockup (importModal): a list of recently imported files (QSettings key recent_lab_files, newest first, max 8, missing files shown greyed) plus the sample labs bundled in the package (desktop/src/practicum_desktop/samples/*.json, byte-identical copies of examples/ guarded by a test), and 'Browse computer…' which opens QFileDialog.getOpenFileName (filter *.json) - the single sanctioned native dialog; picking a file there continues immediately. The same dialog then becomes the staged progress view (importingOverlay): Reading lab file -> Importing lab definition (POST /labs/import via the new ApiClient.import_lab/ImportLabResult) -> Checking host ports (GET /labs/{id}/ports) -> Starting containers (POST /labs/{id}/start). Conflict-free labs start with no further clicks; labs with conflicts (or an unanswerable port check) return gate_required and MainWindow opens PreStartGateDialog for them, so the gate stays the only authority for starting with conflicts. File problems are caught before any API call by lab_file.read_lab_file: missing file, directory, >5 MB, non-UTF-8, JSON syntax error with line/column, non-object JSON, and .zip (no bundle format exists yet - rejected with 'choose the .json export' guidance). API schema errors are listed inline as 'nodes[0].image: Field required' lines (lab_file.format_issue); unsupported schema_version majors (e.g. 2.0) are now rejected server-side by LabDefinition with a readable message. If the API is down the dialog shows a blocked banner pointing at the main window's status/Retry instead of a generic failure. After the dialog closes MainWindow refreshes GET /labs, selects the imported lab, shows 'imported and started' (or 'imported - use Start when ready'), and opens the manual flyout when started - today's equivalent of the running view until windows-desktop-embedded-lab-view exists; re-point _apply_pending_selection when it does. Duplicate imports create a new lab each time (API behaviour; Tigre/09 Q-1 still open). Also fixed on the way: ApiClient.start_lab now uses a 900 s lifecycle timeout (Tigre/06 #3) with a specific timeout message; the runtime and docker_status now treat any OSError from the docker CLI (e.g. PermissionError) as a structured failure instead of a 500 / a dead startup thread. Tests: desktop 105 (+56: test_lab_file 19, test_import_lab 21, test_main_window 7, test_api_client +8, test_docker_status +1; shared tests/qt_helpers.py), core 104 (+4). Exercised end-to-end in a Linux sandbox against a live API (PySide6 offscreen): valid import, schema 2.0 rejection, multi-error file, forced port conflict -> gate, conflict-free -> start failure surfaced with guidance. NOT yet manually verified on Windows - needs one smoke run with Docker Desktop (native picker look, auto-start landing, recent list). Update 2026-10-23 (after the first Windows smoke run hit Tigre/06 #13): the check stage is now 'Checking host ports and networks…' - a subnet overlap with an existing Docker network (typically a leftover from an earlier session) hands over to the gate, which can fix it, instead of failing at start (runtime-subnet-conflicts). Update 2026-10-24: opened from 'Import Existing Lab' on the welcome screen and the dashboard (the old 'Import Lab File…' button is gone); passes source_file; start stage polls real progress; lands on the running view when started.

acceptance_criteria.text: The user can select a lab file via a file-open affordance.
Invalid or malformed files show a clear, specific error and the import does not proceed.
A valid, conflict-free import proceeds straight to the running view without extra clicks.
A valid import with port conflicts stops at the pre-start readiness gate instead of starting.
The imported lab appears in the Labs Dashboard list afterward, whether or not it was started in the same flow.

stories.title: Lab Lifecycle Controls
stories.notes: Done 2026-10-24 (Session 5). RunningLabView (desktop/src/practicum_desktop/running_view.py) is the running-lab screen from the mockup: header with back/title/meta/status badge and the lifecycle toolbar. Running: Restart + Stop lab (unconfirmed) + Reset (kind=danger, always confirmed via dialogs.confirm(destructive=True) with 'more destructive than Stop … cannot be undone') + Instructions toggle. Stopped/Ready/Error: Start lab (through PreStartGateDialog, D-4) + Reset (offered in every state). All lifecycle buttons are disabled while a call is in flight (_busy), the view polls GET /status every second meanwhile and shows the per-node StartProgressPanel, a 409 (busy) is explained as a warning. Confirmed Reset -> POST /reset -> badge Ready + message; manual progress in QSettings untouched (test_reset_keeps_manual_progress); cancel leaves everything unchanged. Backend enablers: runtime-lab-restart (docker start for stopped containers, POST /restart, 409 action lock). Tests: desktop/tests/test_running_view.py (19). E2E against a fake docker CLI (stop -> start via gate -> reset); Windows run pending. Update 2026-10-24: the Windows crash during a quick start with two port overrides (QThread destroyed while running) is fixed at the root by workers.ManagedThread (self-registering threads, D-41); polls skip a tick while the previous one runs.

acceptance_criteria.text: The running-lab view exposes Restart, Stop, and Reset as distinct actions.
Selecting Reset always shows an in-app confirmation before any destructive call is made.
Confirming Reset calls the lab reset endpoint and the UI reflects the lab's returned-to-clean state afterward.
Canceling the Reset confirmation leaves the lab running and unchanged.
Manual progress survives a Reset; it is only cleared by the manual flyout's own Reset Progress action.
Lifecycle controls are disabled while a Start, Stop, Restart or Reset call is in flight on the same lab.

stories.title: Embedded Lab View
stories.notes: Done 2026-10-24 (Session 5). embedded_view.py: EmbeddedLabView hosts a QWebEngineView (D-16; LocalLabPage accepts self-signed certificates for localhost only, D-28) behind a browser chrome (reload, URL, port picker when >1 TCP mapping with the most web-like port preselected, open in system browser). probe_service GETs http://localhost:<port>/ (any status = answering) and falls back to https:// when plain HTTP is garbled (webtop 3001); until the service answers a waiting card retries every 2.5 s. No web ports -> explanation pointing at Open shell; stopped lab -> says so; QtWebEngine missing -> system-browser fallback card. The instructions flyout toggles independently without reloading the page. main.py sets AA_ShareOpenGLContexts. Tests: test_embedded_view.py (13) + running-view cases. Windows run with webtop pending. Update 2026-10-24 (Windows report: nginx 400 'plain HTTP request was sent to HTTPS port' on webtop 3001): probe treats that 400 as a TLS port and retries https; default mapping scores plain-web ports before TLS-only ports (443/8443/3001) regardless of order. First Windows confirmation that the embedded view renders webtop. | 2026-10-25 (user report): several desktops in one lab - the picker lists machines by name from per-node ports in the preview (TopologyNodeInfo.port_mappings / PortMappingInfo.node_id); messages name the machine; the designer gives a second desktop free host ports (free_host_ports).

acceptance_criteria.text: A lab with one browser-accessible node shows that node's interface embedded in the app, not in an external browser.
A lab with multiple browser-accessible nodes lets the user pick which one to view.
The instructions flyout can be opened and closed without losing the embedded view's state.
An open-in-system-browser option is available from the embedded view.

stories.title: Visual Topology Builder (Basic)
stories.notes: Done 2026-10-24 (Session 5). designer.py: DesignerDialog -> DesignerView screen laid out like screen-custom: Machines panel (MachineRow cards: icon/id/image/derived role/remove + add form), Network topology panel (widgets.TopologyView schematic: cards in spec order, connector pills for adjacent machines sharing a network, every interface listed under its machine, orphan networks at the right; interfaces table; connect form), Networks panel (NetworkRow + add form), bottom bar with status pill ('Draft valid · 3 machines · 2 networks' or what is missing) and Validate / Cancel / Save Lab / Save & Start (D-29). Same in-memory draft and API calls; validation messages unchanged and inline; client-side mirrors added for overlapping subnets and network/broadcast addresses. Role derived from interface count (D-27). No drag-and-drop (D-6); in-place edit still S-7. Tests: test_designer.py (14), test_widgets.py.

acceptance_criteria.text: Adding a machine shows it as a card with its id and image.
Adding a network shows it in the networks panel with its id and subnet.
Connecting a machine to a network updates the topology view to show that connection and its subnet label.
Removing a machine, network, or connection updates all affected panels immediately.
Existing Validate and Save behavior, including error messages, is unchanged.

stories.title: Image Pull and Start Progress
stories.notes: Done 2026-10-24 (Session 5). runtime.py: DockerRuntime.start(lab, on_progress) checks each image (docker image inspect) and pulls only missing ones with an explicit streamed `docker pull` (Popen), parsing per-layer status lines into percent + 'n of m layers'; per-node steps waiting/checking_image/pulling_image/creating_container/connecting_networks/ready/failed; failures attributed to the node ('node X (image): could not pull image …'). models.py: NodeStartProgress, RuntimeStatusResult.progress, RuntimeActionResult.pending, Lab.last_error. service.py: progress store, POST /start?wait=false runs on a background thread (202, pending=true), default wait=true unchanged; action lock. Desktop: gate and import start with wait=false and poll GET /status rendering StartProgressPanel / summarize_progress instead of fixed timers; running view shows the panel while starting. Non-TTY docker pull has no byte counts -> layer-based percent. Tests: test_runtime.py (+5), test_api.py (+3), desktop test_progress_panel.py, gate/import/running-view tests. E2E with a fake docker that streams pull output.

acceptance_criteria.text: Lab status exposes a distinguishable in-progress state per node while starting, separate from running/stopped/error.
When a node's image must be pulled, its status includes enough information for the desktop app to show real percentage-style progress.
When a node's image is already local, its status does not show pull progress and moves directly to container startup.
A failed pull or container start is reported against the specific node, with a message distinct from a generic failure.
Existing start/status/stop/reset behavior and endpoints are otherwise unchanged.

stories.title: Restart a Lab and Start After Stop
stories.notes: New 2026-10-24 (was Tigre/11 S-6). DockerRuntime.start uses `docker start` for containers left by Stop (Tigre/06 #2 fixed); LabService.restart + POST /labs/{id}/restart; action lock: start/stop/restart/reset/delete on a starting/stopping lab -> 409 LabBusyError; teardown tolerates 'network X not found' as well as 'No such …' (_is_missing_error). ApiClient.stop_lab/restart_lab/reset_lab share _lifecycle_call (lifecycle timeout, 409 -> busy). Tests in tests/test_api.py, test_runtime.py, test_service.py, desktop/tests/test_api_client.py.

acceptance_criteria.text: Starting a stopped lab reuses its existing containers (docker start) and ends in running.
POST /labs/{lab_id}/restart on a running lab calls stop then start and ends in running; on a stopped or defined lab it just starts it.
A lifecycle call made while the lab is starting or stopping is rejected with 409 and leaves the lab's status unchanged.
Resetting a lab whose networks were already removed outside Practicum succeeds.

stories.title: Delete a Lab Through the API
stories.notes: New 2026-10-24 (was Tigre/11 S-4). DELETE /labs/{id} -> 204; never-started labs skip Docker; otherwise runtime reset first, failure keeps the lab (status error, last_error) and answers 409 (D-25); 404 unknown; 409 while busy. ApiClient.delete_lab (DeleteResult, 404 = already gone). Dashboard Delete uses it after confirm(). Tests: tests/test_api.py test_delete_*, desktop test_api_client/test_main_window. Update 2026-10-24: delete always resets the lab's Docker names; startup lifespan sweep + POST /docker/sweep-leftovers remove Practicum-labelled resources of labs this API does not know (D-40).

acceptance_criteria.text: Deleting a running lab removes its Docker resources and the lab; GET /labs no longer lists it.

stories.title: Lab Origin and Activity Timestamps

Stored Lab gains origin (designer|imported|quick_start), source_file, created_at, last_started_at, last_error; set via POST /labs?origin= and POST /labs/import?source_file=, updated by lifecycle actions; excluded from export and preserved by port/subnet recommendations (LAB_RUNTIME_FIELDS, LabService._with_definition). Desktop LabSummary parses them; labels.py words the card meta/activity lines. Resolves Q-6.

acceptance_criteria.text: A created, quick-started and imported lab each report the matching origin (and source_file for the import) from GET /labs.
The exported spec of any lab contains none of the bookkeeping fields.
last_started_at is set after a successful start and last_error is cleared; a failed action sets last_error.
Applying a port or subnet recommendation keeps origin, source_file and created_at.

acceptance_criteria.text: All six screens render inside the one window with the title bar and status chip.

stories.title: Create New Lab Screen

acceptance_criteria.text: Adding and removing packages updates the chips and the status pill; invalid names are rejected inline.

stories.title: Machine Catalogue for the Custom Lab Designer
stories.notes: New 2026-10-24 (user feedback: 'images of nodes to pre-select from … daisy chain machines'). node_catalog.py PRESETS: Ubuntu host, Alpine host, Router (alpine + sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward=1), Web server (nginx, 8080→80, command kept), Ubuntu Desktop (webtop 3000/3001), Custom image; NodePreset.node() builds the full node; next_node_id suggests host-1/router-1…; suggest_address pre-fills the connect form (routers .1, hosts from .10; skips network/broadcast/Docker gateway/taken) and an address reference line + per-network 'machine · address' rows answer 'a reference for the hosts ips'. stories.title: Windows Container Readiness for Quick Start
stories.notes: Done 2026-10-25 (Session 6). Read-only `docker info --format '{{json .}}'` in both the desktop (`docker_status.check_docker` -> DockerStatus.os_type/host_build/isolation; `windows_container_readiness()` -> docker_unavailable | linux_engine | ready with detail + next_action) and the API (`GET /docker/engine`, `DockerRuntime.engine_info()`, `DockerEngineInfo`). Gate: new 'Container engine' panel blocks Start + Retry; import flow hands a mismatched lab to the gate; `POST /start` re-checks server-side with the switch instructions. NOT yet verified on a Windows machine.

acceptance_criteria.text: The app distinguishes an unavailable Docker daemon, a Linux-container daemon, and a Windows-container daemon.

stories.title: Windows Quick Start Template
stories.notes: Done 2026-10-25 (Session 6). Spec: `Node.os` (linux|windows) + `Node.shell` (bash|sh|powershell|cmd), validated (one OS per lab, shell fits OS, no shm/sysctls on Windows); `LabDefinition.container_os`, `LabPreview.container_os`. Template `windows` (kind windows, 2 vCPU/2048 MB, one `host` node): image pinned from `WINDOWS_IMAGES` (ltsc2025>=26100, ltsc2022>=20348, ltsc2019>=17763) by the daemon host's build (`windows_image_for_host`, `QuickStartDraft.windows_host_build`; unknown -> ltsc2022; older hosts refused). acceptance_criteria.text: The Windows template is selectable only when Windows-container readiness passes.

stories.title: Open a PowerShell Shell on a Windows Lab Node
stories.notes: Done 2026-10-25 (Session 6). `node_shell.shell_command(container, os, shell)` from the declared os/shell (preview -> TopologyNodeInfo.os/shell): Linux keeps bash-then-sh (or the declared one), Windows runs `powershell.exe -NoLogo -ExecutionPolicy Bypass` (or `cmd.exe`); no spaces/quotes in any argument. `open_node_shell` pre-checks `docker inspect` state and returns an actionable in-app error for stopped/missing containers (no flashing console). Running view: 'Open PowerShell' (terminal icon) on Windows nodes, tooltip/accessible name/status line name node and shell. Spec field => survives export/import (core test). Tests: test_node_shell (10), test_running_view, test_api_client. Tigre/06 #14 (console launch unverified on Windows) still applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: Open shell on a running Windows Quick Start node opens an interactive PowerShell prompt inside that container.

stories.title: Choose Windows Tools in Quick Start
stories.notes: Done 2026-10-25 (Session 6). `WINDOWS_TOOL_CATALOG`: 15 Chocolatey ids (git, python, nodejs-lts, dotnet-sdk, openjdk, powershell-core, 7zip, curl, wget, jq, vim, nano, openssh, sqlite, sysinternals) offered only for the windows kind; kind-aware `catalog_option`/`packages_for_options`. Picker reuses the chip UI with Windows wording; custom ids validated as Chocolatey ids (lower-cased, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$`, link to community.chocolatey.org), duplicates rejected. Mechanism: `WINDOWS_INIT_SCRIPT` installs Chocolatey then `choco install <id> -y --no-progress` per package (failures name the package), log `C:\practicum\packages.log`; packages are explicit in `environment.PRACTICUM_PACKAGES` (+ `PRACTICUM_PACKAGE_SOURCE=chocolatey`), image pinned. Status marker `C:\practicum\packages.status` -> `GET /status` note (core reads it per OS) -> Lab nodes table 'installing…'/'install failed' + PowerShell profile banner. Ubuntu apt/LinuxServer paths untouched. Tests: test_quickstart, test_create_lab, core test_runtime. NOT yet verified on Windows (Chocolatey in Server Core needs internet + .NET 4.8).

acceptance_criteria.text: Catalog tools and custom package IDs are available for Windows Quick Start and validated before creation.
The generated lab installs selected tools through a documented, repeatable Windows-specific mechanism.
Package installation progress and failures are visible in the existing node progress/status UI.

stories.title: Use Design Icons Across the Desktop UI
stories.notes: Done 2026-10-25 (Session 6). `icons.py` maps the 3x3 sheet to meanings (success/error/warning, back/forward/play, terminal/desktop/tools) with BANNER_ICONS/COLOUR_ICONS aliases; `tools/slice_design_icons.py` cuts design/icons.png into assets/icons/*.png (coloured icons keep white glyphs via edge flood fill; black icons stored as ink masks for tinting). Loaders: icon()/pixmap()/icon_label()/set_button_icon()/icon_html(), cached, multi-size, tint + disabled states, null-safe when assets are missing. Applied: MessageBanner (icon + copyable text) replaces every plain banner label (gate, running view, designer, welcome, NoteBanner), StatusPill, title chip + connection lines, progress marks, flyout done markers + Mark step complete, Start/Save & Start/Start Lab (play), Open shell/PowerShell (terminal), BackLinks, Create cards/template rows, CTA trailing arrows, dashboard origin tiles, embedded empty state, readiness + engine panels. Icon-only controls carry tooltip + accessibleName; every state also has words. Packaging: --add-data for practicum_desktop/assets (+samples) in build-windows.ps1 and Practicum.spec; ICON_DIRS checks sys._MEIPASS. Side fix: dashboard cards with an error line were clipped (minimumHeight from sizeHint). Tests: test_icons (8), test_widgets, screen tests; offscreen screenshots reviewed. Not checked on a real high-DPI display / packaged build yet.

acceptance_criteria.text: The supplied icons are mapped to their intended meanings in shared icon definitions.

Icons render legibly in the packaged Windows app and missing assets do not prevent launch or primary workflows.
